definition.given: A reviewer has two work items with different descriptions. The full-page details of EDIT-1 [EDIT-1:title] Prepare launch brief are open, showing its identifier, title, and launch-goals description.
definition.when: The reviewer uses Search commands to open EDIT-2 [EDIT-2:title] Review research notes, then uses Search commands to return to EDIT-1 [EDIT-1:title] Prepare launch brief.
definition.observed: The identifier and title return to "EDIT-1 [EDIT-1:title] Prepare launch brief", but the description input still shows "[EDIT-2:desc] Summarize customer interviews and capture the key findings.", the description from EDIT-2.
definition.require: The selected work item's identifier, title, description, and other item-specific details all belong to that item. Returning to a previously viewed item restores its own description and editor context.
allow: Loading indicators, skeletons, or blank transitions may appear while the selected item's details load. Visible item-specific content belongs to the selection it is presented under.
Unsaved edits may be autosaved, retained separately per item, discarded after a prompt, or handled before a switch. Their ownership remains clear.
List order, layout, wording, and editor implementation may vary.
After rapid switches, settled details correspond to the last confirmed selection.

theory.title: Direct item retrieval - Opening a search result displays that item's complete details
theory.reference: Designing Interfaces, Third Edition, Chapter 7: Lists of Things; designing-interfaces/chapters/ch07-lists.md
theory.rationale: Search commands lets the reviewer jump directly between named work items. Each destination's identifier, title, and description should refer to that same item, including when revisiting an earlier result.

theory.title: Interactions Are Conversations - The system must coherently and completely acknowledge the user's selection
theory.reference: Designing Interfaces, Third Edition, Chapter 1: Designing for People; designing-interfaces/chapters/ch01-designing-for-people.md
theory.rationale: Selecting EDIT-1 [EDIT-1:title] Prepare launch brief requests that item's details. The interface may show loading first, then presents its identifier, title, and description together as the selected item's content.

reference_observation: Selecting EDIT-2 [EDIT-2:title] Review research notes displays its research description. Returning to EDIT-1 [EDIT-1:title] Prepare launch brief restores its launch-goals description under the correct identifier and title.
requirement_rationale: A reviewer uses the selected work item's details to assess that item. Keeping descriptions and editor context attached to the correct item makes returning to an earlier selection reliable.
